title: Lunar: The Silver Star
subtitle: A boy who dreams of dragons
summary: Lunar: The Silver Star is Game Arts and Studio Alex's role-playing adventure, first released for Mega-CD in Japan on 26 June 1992.
body: Lunar: The Silver Star is Game Arts and Studio Alex's role-playing adventure, first released for Mega-CD in Japan on 26 June 1992. Alex, a boy who admires the legendary Dragonmaster Dyne, leaves his small town on an adventure that grows into a struggle for Lunar's future. Companions join him as he explores settlements and dangerous places, learns about the dragons and works towards his own place in that history. The CD format gives the journey animated scenes, spoken passages and recorded music, adding another presence to its illustrated fantasy world.

Battles occur during exploration and use turn-based commands, with the characters' speed determining when actions take place. Position also matters: a fighter must reach an enemy to strike, while ranged attacks can cross that distance. The player can move a character, hold ground or retreat, making the battlefield more than a list of opposing statistics. Weapons and equipment found along the route improve the party's effectiveness. Experience from victories strengthens the group, allowing it to face the increasingly dangerous creatures encountered as Alex's journey reaches further from home.

Artist Toshiyuki Kubooka designed the characters, while Noriyuki Iwadare, Hiroshi Fujioka and Isao Mizoguchi contributed the music. Short animated and audio interludes give important moments another form alongside the ordinary conversations and exploration. Working Designs localised the game for North America in 1993, bringing that CD-based presentation to an English-speaking audience. Its success established the Lunar series before Eternal Blue continued the world in another era. The original's central appeal joins a familiar coming-of-age adventure to the sound and moving images that the new disc hardware could place around its characters.
